title: the impact of surgical research on career success
display_name: The Impact of Surgical Research on Career Success
abstract: in 1957 the department of surgery at the university of louisville school of medicine received a gift from dr. john w. price and his wife, barbara thruston atwood price, to create a surgical research unit. the unit was named the price institute of surgical research (pisr). the corpus of the gift was placed in a bank of which dr. price was a longtime board member, where it has remained and continued to grow. a fundamental purpose of this trust was to support the salary of a research fellow. the first of these fellows was alex haller jr. while in louisville, he was full-time pediatric surgical faculty including cardiac surgery. dr. haller had a very distinguished career, and subsequently founded children's surgery at johns hopkins hospital in baltimore. a majority of the subsequent 56 research fellows have been international, arriving at the pisr after completing medical school, and in the earlier part of their surgical residency. beginning in 1991, many of these fellows earned a phd from the university of louisville department of physiology, a practice that continues on to this day. these pisr fellows have been appointed from around the world, coming from 14 different countries and various academic institutions, including the university of louisville. the fellows are chosen based on strong personal recommendations from surgical leaders around the world. with 7 exceptions, all fellows have returned to, or near, their home country to complete their subsequent careers. additionally, 9 fellows have progressed to either department chair, director of a major surgical division, or dean. three fellows have become editor-in-chief of peer-reviewed surgical journals. the current director of the pisr (sg) is full time faculty in the department of surgery, as are all former institute directors. these individuals directly teach and mentor research fellows and students in the laboratory. some of the director's income is derived from the department and its associated group practice. the price institute is largely financially independent; none of its funds are used for faculty compensation. due to competent management and the price trust's generosity, the pisr has developed into an active and successful research unit. this development has caused the lab to attract, in addition to fellows, undergraduate students with many wishing to take steps towards a medical career. students the purpose of this report is to describe the experience of undergraduate students who completed summer research electives at this surgical research unit and their subsequent career choices. since the pisr's establishment, 108 undergraduate students have worked in the unit. of these 108 students, 16% were a racial or religious minority and 38% were women. the authors excluded students who entered the unit as medical students, because there is already substantial literature as to the effect of medical student research.1 5 early on, many students who came to work in the laboratory were encouraged to do so by relatives who knew of their interest in medicine or science, and thought it might be a worthy path upon which to begin. therefore, the role of student involvement in the lab has been a subject of slow growth across the 80's and 90's, largely by word of mouth. additionally, expectations of students have grown over time. along with the original expectations of hard work and hands-on science, students are now expected to give formal presentations at lab meetings, present at national meetings, assist with manuscript writing, submission, resubmission, and be listed as coauthor (and even first-author on occasion). such expectations have allowed many students to achieve their goal of matriculating into medical school or other graduate schools. student experience survey recently, the authors set out to more closely examine undergraduate student research experiences at the unit, for the purpose of creating a more beneficial research experience. of the 108 students, 2 are deceased. therefore, data regarding summer student research electives were available for 106 undergraduate students from 1980 to date, allowing students to be traced from their initial research experience to their current career. such long-term follow-up data is notably absent in many discussions of surgical education. additionally, the authors sent anonymized surveys to these students to assess the quality of their research experience and the impact of the experience on their careers. the university of louisville institutional review board deemed this survey exempt from full review and approval. results the 106 students consisted of 6 high school, 96 collegiate, and 4 graduate students. collegiate students either graduated with a bachelors/associates degree with no further schooling or were still enrolled in college when beginning research. not surprisingly to our senior authors, of the 96 contacted students, 75% (n = 72/96) matriculated into medical school (table 1: left). of accepted students, 36% are female and 17% are from groups underrepresented in medicine. matriculation into medical school did not differ between groups [46/66 men (70%), 26/40 women (65%); 12/17 racial or religious minority students (71%), 60/89 white students (67%), p > 0.5, 2 for all comparisons]. however, it was surprising that 32% (23/72) of those admitted into medical school chose careers in general surgery or a major surgical specialty (orthopedic, otolaryngologic, or urologic surgery). to find a comparable group, we were able to obtain data on residency selection from the university of louisville school of medicine from 2000 to 2019. therefore, pisr students who graduated before 2000 or who had not yet chosen a residency were excluded from this comparison. after this exclusion, 33% (11/33) of pisr students chose a career in a surgical specialty compared to 14% of the university of louisville school of medicine graduates as a whole who chose careers in similar surgical specialties. although this may reflect some degree of self-selection, it certainly is a positive outcome. therefore, it may be warranted to look further into the role of surgical research before medical school as a means to attract medical students into surgical careers. table 1 - pisr student profile and survey responses (n = 60/96) specialities number of students (%) question stem strongly agree/agree (%) neither agree/disagree (%) strongly disagree/disagree (%) other (%) residencies/status of students accepted to medical school (n = 72) laboratory skills development surgical specialties improved interpretation of scientific data 95 5 0 0 general surgery 15 (21) improved understanding of research process 98 0 2 medicine 2 (3) diagnostic radiology 2 (3) obstetrics-gynecology 2 (3) family medicine 1 (1) gastroenterology 1 (1) pathology 1 (1) physical medicine & rehabilitation 1 (1) total 37 (52) currently in medical school 12 (16) pisr indicates price institute of surgical research. of 106 students, 96 could be contacted and were sent a survey. the survey had a very acceptable 63% response rate (60/96). table 1 (right) shows the results of the likert-scale questions. over 90% of students strongly agreed/agreed that the experience improved laboratory skills such as data interpretation and understanding the research process. relating to professional development, over 85% of respondents strongly agreed/agreed that the experience improved and/or assisted their presentation skills, professional skills, or professional connections. lastly, over 80% of students strongly agreed/agreed that the experience helped with developing their careers. the survey also inquired how long a student participated in research and revealed that 70% of students were involved in research for more than 1 summer. this continued research involvement over multiple summers is reflected in the large number of publications with student co-authorships or even first authorships (n = 163), with 61% of the 106 students having at least 1 peer-reviewed publication. additionally, 9 students have at least 1 paper as first author. conclusions the data presented in this report demonstrates the value of exposure to surgical research to undergraduate students, and specifically exposure to research in the pisr. the unique nature of this report is that these students were undergraduates when beginning their research experience, and the availability of long-term follow-up data, including their subsequent careers. this paper may reflect an area of further study for not only surgical education, but also for medical education overall. matriculation into medical school grows more competitive each year, as does matching into a surgical residency and/or fellowship. research is a common route students take to enhance their applications, with evidence that research participation does influence medical school matriculation.6 additionally, evidence has shown that research during residency impacts surgeons future career paths.7 due to the impact this research experience and exposure had on these students and their future careers, it is important that research electives provide students the opportunity to better themselves personally and professionally. our data reflect that the majority of students had a generally positive experience, and that 75% attended medical school. although the survey responses and students career choices cannot be directly correlated, the responses show that the experience helped 92% of students achieve their career goals and motivated 82% to pursue their current/previous career. such results indicate that the experience did impact students future careers. additionally, our students residency choices show that surgical research opportunities, before medical school, could be helpful as a means to recruit students towards surgical specialties. the results of this study may provide insight into practices that create positive student research experiences, thereby encouraging student involvement in research. this involvement allows students to accumulate publications and improve their qualifications as applicants for medical school, residency, fellowship, or for subsequent faculty roles. in conclusion, this paper offers a study of a surgical research unit that has been operating for 60 years. the ability to look back over such a long period of time may provide today's academic institutions and researchers with ideas on how to improve their own students research experiences. it may also spark additional studies to take this study a step further, and examine how early research participation specifically impacts the career choices of this selected body of students.

title: meniscectomy
display_name: Meniscectomy
abstract: to review the meniscus from a historical perspective especially on surgical management and general guidelines for arthroscopic meniscectomy procedures for various types of meniscal tears. we searched medline and pubmed for the years of 1980-2010 using the terms meniscus, meniscal repair, menisectomy, and arthroscopy. orthopedic surgeons frequently encounter patients with pain or functional impairment of the knee joint and repair or resection of the injured meniscus is one of the most common orthopedic operative procedures. the object of meniscal surgery is to reduce pain, restore functional meniscus and prevent the development of degenerative osteoarthritis in the involved knee. historically, total meniscectomy was a common procedure performed for meniscus tear symptoms. however, it has been reported that total meniscectomy has deleterious effects on the knee. in the past, the menisci were thought as a functionless remnant tissue. currently, it is known that the meniscus is an important structure for knee joint function. menisci provide several vital functions including mechanical support, localized pressure distribution, and lubrication to the knee joint. it is widely accepted that the function of the meniscus can be preserved through minimal excision. an arthroscopic partial meniscectomy preserving more of the meniscus is preferred over total meniscectomy. in recent decades, this shift toward arthroscopic partial meniscectomy has led to the development of new surgical techniques.

title: interrater agreement between telerehabilitation and face-to-face clinical outcome measurements for total knee arthroplasty
display_name: Interrater Agreement Between Telerehabilitation and Face-to-Face Clinical Outcome Measurements for Total Knee Arthroplasty

authorships.name: François Cabana
institutions: Health and Social Services Centre University Institute of Geriatrics of Sherbrooke

authorships.name: Patrick Boissy
institutions: Health and Social Services Centre University Institute of Geriatrics of Sherbrooke

authorships.name: Michel Tousignant
institutions: Health and Social Services Centre University Institute of Geriatrics of Sherbrooke

authorships.name: Hélène Corriveau
institutions: Health and Social Services Centre University Institute of Geriatrics of Sherbrooke

abstract: outcome measures in physical therapy provide the basis for determining the patient's rehabilitation needs, developing an individual intervention plan, and reassessing the evolution of the condition after therapeutic intervention. questions surrounding the validity and reliability of outcome measures obtained in the context of telerehabilitation remain. the goal of this study was to explore which outcome measures can be used reliably in the context of telerehabilitation after discharge from an acute care hospital for lower limb orthopedic surgery. fifteen patients recently discharged after total knee arthroplasty were evaluated by two experienced therapists. each therapist evaluated under a given condition (face-to-face assessment, telerehabilitation assessment) eight outcome measures taken from standard clinical tests routinely used in the management of orthopedic rehabilitation after total knee arthroplasty. evaluations were measured at 1-day intervals. telerehabilitation evaluations were conducted with a videoconference link (h.264 codecs with pan, tilt, zoom cameras) between either the participant's home or a clinical environment and a remote clinical station over residential dsl lines at 512 kbps. interrater agreement between the two measurement modes was analyzed using the bland and altman method and kripendorff's alpha reliability estimate. the 95% confidence interval for mean difference between evaluation methods varied between -20% and 8% for knee range of motion measures, -85% and 55% for scar management, -33% and 29% for functional evaluations. five out of the eight outcome measures showed reliability estimates of >0.80, with lowest reliability obtained for the scar assessment scale (0.34) and the highest reliability for the evaluation of the range of motion at the knee (0.87 in flexion and 0.85 in extension). clinical variables typically measured in face-to-face evaluations can be measured successfully under telerehabilitation conditions with moderate reliability.

title: management of bone disease in cystinosis: statement from an international conference
display_name: Management of bone disease in cystinosis: Statement from an international conference
abstract: abstract cystinosis is an autosomal recessive storage disease due to impaired transport of cystine out of lysosomes. since the accumulation of intracellular cystine affects all organs and tissues, the management of cystinosis requires a specialized multidisciplinary team consisting of pediatricians, nephrologists, nutritionists, ophthalmologists, endocrinologists, neurologists' geneticists, and orthopedic surgeons. treatment with cysteamine can delay or prevent most clinical manifestations of cystinosis, except the renal fanconi syndrome. virtually all individuals with classical, nephropathic cystinosis suffer from cystinosis metabolic bone disease (cmbd), related to the renal fanconi syndrome in infancy and progressive chronic kidney disease (ckd) later in life. manifestations of cmbd include hypophosphatemic rickets in infancy, and renal osteodystrophy associated with ckd resulting in bone deformities, osteomalacia, osteoporosis, fractures, and short stature. assessment of cmbd involves monitoring growth, leg deformities, blood levels of phosphate, electrolytes, bicarbonate, calcium, and alkaline phosphatase, periodically obtaining bone radiographs, determining levels of critical hormones and vitamins, such as thyroid hormone, parathyroid hormone, 25(oh) vitamin d, and testosterone in males, and surveillance for nonrenal complications of cystinosis such as myopathy. treatment includes replacement of urinary losses, cystine depletion with oral cysteamine, vitamin d, hormone replacement, physical therapy, and corrective orthopedic surgery. the recommendations in this article came from an expert meeting on cmbd that took place in salzburg, austria, in december 2016.

title: is the asa score in geriatric hip fractures a predictive factor for complications and readmission?
display_name: Is the ASA Score in Geriatric Hip Fractures a Predictive Factor for Complications and Readmission?
abstract: hip fractures are the second cause of hospitalization in geriatric patients. the american society of anesthesiologists (asa) classification scheme is a scoring system for the evaluation of the patients health and comorbidities before an operative procedure. the purpose of this study was to determine whether the asa score is a predictive factor for perioperative and postoperative complications and a cause of readmission of geriatric patients with hip fractures. the study included 198 elderly patients. the mean values of hospitalization were 6.4 2.1 days for the patients with asa ii, 10.4 3.4 days for the patients with asa iii, and 13.5 4.4 days for the patients with asa iv. the patients with asa ii exhibited minor complications, while patients with asa iii presented cutaneous ulcer and respiratory dysfunction. five patients with asa iv had pulmonary embolism, two patients had myocardial infarction, and three patients died. the asa score seems to have direct correlation with multiple factors, such as the hospitalization days, the severity of the complications, and the total hospitalization costs. the treatment of geriatrics hip fractures in patients with a high asa score requires a multidisciplinary approach and a special assessment in order to decrease postoperative morbidity and mortality and offer optimal functionality.

title: patients experiences of discontentment one year after total knee arthroplasty- a qualitative study
display_name: Patients’ experiences of discontentment one year after total knee arthroplasty- a qualitative study
abstract: abstract background total knee arthroplasty is a common procedure with generally good results. however, there are still patients who are dissatisfied without known explanation. satisfaction and dissatisfaction have previously been captured by quantitative designs, but there is a lack of qualitative studies regarding these patients experiences. qualitative knowledge might be useful in creating strategies to decrease the dissatisfaction rate. methods of the 348 patients who responded to a letter asking if they were satisfied or dissatisfied with their surgery, 61 (18%) reported discontent. after excluding patients with documented complications and those who declined to participate, semi-structured interviews were conducted with 44 patients. the interviews were analyzed according to qualitative content analysis. the purpose was to describe patients experiences of discontentment 1 year after total knee arthroplasty. results the patients experienced unfulfilled expectations and needs regarding unresolved and new problems, limited independence, and lacking of relational supports. they were bothered by pain and stiffness, and worried that changes were complications as a result of surgery. they described inability to perform daily activities and valued activities. they also felt a lack of relational supports, and a lack of respect and continuity, support from health care, and information adapted to their needs. conclusion patient expectation seems to be the major contributing factor in patient discontentment after knee replacement surgery. this qualitative study sheds light on the on the meaning of unfulfilled expectations, in contrast to previous quantitative studies. the elements of unfulfilled expectations need to be dealt with both on the individual staff level and on the organizational level. for instance, increased continuity of healthcare staff and facilities may help to improve patient satisfaction after surgery.

title: effects of innovative virtual reality game and emg biofeedback on neuromotor control in cerebral palsy
display_name: Effects of innovative virtual reality game and EMG biofeedback on neuromotor control in cerebral palsy
abstract: sensorimotor control dysfunction or dyskinesia is a hallmark of neuromuscular impairment in children with cerebral palsy (cp), and is often implicated in reaching and grasping deficiencies due to a neuromuscular imbalance between the triceps and biceps. to mitigate such muscle imbalances, an innovative electromyography (emg)-virtual reality (vr) biofeedback system were designed to provide accurate information about muscle activation and motivation. however, the clinical efficacy of this approach has not yet been determined in children with cp. the purpose of this study was to investigate the effectiveness of a combined emg biofeedback and vr (emg-vr biofeedback) intervention system to improve muscle imbalance between triceps and biceps during reaching movements in children with spastic cp. raw emg signals were recorded at a sampling rate of 1,000 hz, band-pass filtered between 20 450 hz, and notch-filtered at 60 hz during elbow flexion and extension movements. emg data were then processed using myoresearch master edition 1.08 xp software. all participants underwent both interventions consisting of the emg-vr biofeedback combination and emg biofeedback alone. emg analysis resulted in improved muscle activation in the underactive triceps while decreasing overactive or hypertonic biceps in the emg-vr biofeedback compared with emg biofeedback. the muscle imbalance ratio between the triceps and biceps was consistently improved. the present study is the first clinical trial to provide evidence for the additive benefits of vr intervention for enhancing the upper limb function of children with spastic cp.

title: acute neurosurgical management of traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury in french armed forces during deployment
display_name: Acute neurosurgical management of traumatic brain injury and spinal cord injury in French armed forces during deployment
abstract: this article aims to describe the french concept regarding combat casualty neurosurgical care from the theater of operations to a homeland hospital. french military neurosurgeons are not routinely deployed to all combat zones. as a consequence, general surgeons initially treat neurosurgical wounds. the principle of this medical support is based on damage control. it is aimed at controlling intracranial hypertension spikes when neuromonitoring is lacking in resource-limited settings. neurosurgical damage control permits a medevac that is as safe as can be expected from a conflict zone to a homeland medical treatment facility. french military neurosurgeons can occasionally be deployed within an airborne team to treat a military casualty or to complete a neurosurgical procedure performed by a general surgeon in theaters of operation. all surgeons regardless of their specialty must know neurosurgical damage control. general surgeons must undergo the required training in order for them to perform this neurosurgical technique.

title: biopolymers for hard and soft engineered tissues: application in odontoiatric and plastic surgery field
display_name: Biopolymers for Hard and Soft Engineered Tissues: Application in Odontoiatric and Plastic Surgery Field
abstract: the goal of modern dentistry and plastic surgery is to restore the patient to normal function, health and aesthetics, regardless of the disease or injury to the stomatognathic and cutaneous system respectively. in recent years tissue engineering and regenerative medicine have yielded many novel tissue replacements and implementation strategies. scientific advances in biomaterials, stem cell isolation, growth and differentiation factors and biomimetic environments have created unique opportunities to fabricate tissues in the laboratory. repairing of bone and skin is likely to become of clinical interest when three dimensional tissue reconstructive procedures and the appropriate supporting biomimetic materials are correctly assembled. in the present review, we provide an overview of the most promising biopolymers that may find clinical application in dento-maxillo-facial and plastic surgery.

title: pain in children and adolescents with spina bifida
display_name: Pain in children and adolescents with spina bifida

authorships.name: Christine Clancy
institutions: University College Hospital Macmillan Cancer Centre

abstract: the pediatric pain questionnaire and relevant medical records were used to investigate the frequency, intensity, location, and duration of pain experienced by children with spina bifida and to examine the concordance between child self-report and parent proxy report of pain. there were 68 children with spina bifida (30 males, 38 females) between the ages of 8 and 19 years (mean age 12y 8m). fifty-nine children (87%) were diagnosed with myelomeningocele, six (9%) with lipomyelomeningocele, and three (4%) with lipomeningocele (4%). forty-nine children (72%) had shunted hydrocephalus. twenty-six children (38%) ambulated full-time. fifty-six per cent of children reported experiencing pain once a week or more often. for these children, pain occurred most frequently in the head, back, abdomen, neck, shoulders, legs, and hands. of the 49 children with shunted hydrocephalus, 43 (88%) reported headaches; 15 of 19 children (79%) without hydrocephalus reported headaches. children who reported more intense pain also reported more frequent pain and more pain locations. parents were most reliable at reporting locations of their children's severe pain. parents of younger children significantly underestimated their children's current pain and worst pain in the past 7 days. lesion level and ambulatory status were not associated with any of the pain variables. it was concluded that children with spina bifida frequently report clinically significant, yet under-recognized and untreated pain.
